activity.title: Congratulations 🥳🥳

A few weeks ago, I graduated from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign with a B.S. in Computer Science, a minor in Statistics, and a 3.91 GPA, specializing in computer security and distributed systems. Graduating in 3 years and starting a full-time job at the age of 19, has surprisingly always been part of the plan. What wasn't part of the plan was how much I changed, personally and professionally, over those three years, and the number of people who inspired me, mentored me, and continue to instill their values in me. The first thing I did freshman year was apply to every club I thought was even slightly cool at UIUC, and it led me to some amazing things. I consulted on projects for Fortune 500 companies as part of Illinois Business Consulting , met startup founders through Zero2One VC , and socially, I loved being part of the honors societies Tau Beta Pi - Illinois Zeta The Engineering Honor Society and Alpha Omega Epsilon Sorority Wanting more hands-on research experience, I found incredible mentors in Professor Geoffrey Herman , with whom I did research and learned more about the education industry, and Professor Ryan Cunningham, under whom I served as a Course Assistant for Ethics in Computing. I also served as a Course Assistant for Data Structures (CS225) under Professor Brad Solomon . Their values continue to inspire me. I've changed a lot along the way, but the biggest lesson UIUC taught me was nothing is unachievable if you try hard enough. More than any class, it taught me to stay determined and work for what I want, and everything I have today, I have because of that. Finally, thank you to my amazing family and friends for believing in me. I'm beyond excited to return full-time to Slack ( Salesforce ) as an Android Software Engineer, under the mentorship of Jerrell Mardis , someone who has inspired me not just in my career, but personally too. A huge shoutout to Futureforce: Salesforce University Recruiting and my recruiter Christina Fromson for making this happen. Looking forward to keep building on Android and growing under his mentorship. #NewGrad #Slack #AndroidDev #UIUC

Last week I completed my internship with Jacaranda Flame Consulting - University of Sydney (JFC), one of the most valuable experiences of my degree so far. Our team had the opportunity to work with Unleash live on a real-world engineering project, designing a solar-powered electrical enclosure system complete with full documentation for replication. We presented our final solution directly to Unleash Live at their headquarters, a moment that made the six weeks of work feel very real. My responsibilities centred around mechanical design, thermal management, and assembly planning. Working within a multidisciplinary team taught me just as much as the technical work itself; learning how to divide responsibilities, communicate progress, and bring different skill sets together toward one deliverable is something no coursework unit can fully prepare you for. What I'll take away most from this experience isn't the technical knowledge, though there was plenty of that. It's the professional skills: running client meetings, presenting engineering decisions to a senior audience, and learning to deliver under real constraints and real expectations. These are the things that turn an engineering student into an engineer. I'm grateful to my teammates ( Sharine Helen Precilla , Ningcheng Luo , Vandanaa Sugumaran ) for bringing their best throughout the project, to our supervisor John McCallum for his guidance, and to Kush Shrestha and the Unleash Live team for trusting us with a genuine brief and engaging so generously with our solution. And a big thank you to JFC USYD for creating this opportunity. I'd encourage any engineering student at USYD to apply. You won't regret it. #Engineering #Internship #JFC #UniversityOfSydney #MechanicalEngineering #ProfessionalDevelopment #UnleashLive

From battery recycling to AI-powered manufacturing, Vedant Mohata is tackling a wide range of projects this summer. A senior studying Materials Science and Engineering with minors in Mathematics and Electrical Engineering, Vedant is spending his summer as a Refining Materials Strategy & TPM Intern at Redwood Materials . His work spans three different teams, including lithium recycling from black mass, machine learning-powered battery sorting, and manufacturing strategy, giving him a broad perspective on sustainable battery production and operations. One of the most exciting parts of Vedant’s internship has been diving into AI with little prior experience and learning how to build a battery sorting system from the ground up. Along the way, he’s also developed project management skills while coordinating work across multiple teams. When he’s not at work, you’ll likely find him exploring the national parks around Reno. His advice for students: “Talk to people. You never know when it might come in handy.” We’re proud to spotlight Vedant and look forward to seeing where his passion for sustainable materials and manufacturing takes him! #NationalInternDay #MaterialsScience #BatteryRecycling #Sustainability #UIUC #Keramos #SustainableMaterials

This October, I'll be running the 2026 Bank of America Chicago Marathon with Team MMRF to support the Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation. I'm taking on this challenge because multiple myeloma has affected millions including my friends and family. I want to do my part to help fund the research that's bringing new treatments and hope to all of those affected. Over the past few months, I've been training for the marathon, and I'll continue putting in the miles leading up to race day while working toward my fundraising goal of $3,000. Every donation helps fund research, support clinical trials, and move us closer to better treatments and ultimately a cure. If you're able to support this cause, I'd be incredibly grateful. If you're unable to donate, sharing this post would also help spread awareness. You can learn more about why this cause means so much to me and make a donation here: https://lnkd.in/g73Bbv36 Thank you to everyone who supports this journey. #ChicagoMarathon #MMRF #MultipleMyeloma #CancerResearch #Fundraising #TeamMMRF

Y Combinator flew me out to SF, and I just had the best weekend at Startup School. My main takeaways from Startup School: • Jensen Huang : approach every new problem with "how hard can it be?" • Sam Altman: get comfortable with people calling your idea dumb, or not liking it at all • Jeff Dean : thought experiments are one of the most underrated tools for building systems that matter • Garry Tan : be earnest I would like to thank fellow University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign alum & General Partner at YC, Pete Koomen , for extending the invite. I had cold-emailed him a while back, and that email turning into an invite for Startup School is something I am very grateful for. Beyond that, just getting to spend two days surrounded by builders from every kind of background, different countries, different industries, and different stages of their journey, was genuinely energizing. #ycstartupschool

Your smartest coworker has amnesia AI got smarter but somehow, I kept getting better at repeating myself Every new chat starts the same way: - here's who I am - here’s what I’m working on - here’s how I like things written - here’s the decision we already made Then I close the tab and do it all again tomorrow :( So, we built Cortex! Cortex gives AI a memory of your work it keeps useful context from your conversations, projects, and decisions then brings it back when you need it You can pick up where you left off Cortex already knows the work, the history & how you tend to think And yes, there are a lot of startups trying to solve for this issue and that's why we are open-sourcing Cortex Use it, pull it apart, improve it, or build something strange with it can't wait to see what you do with it :)) (link in comments! and my github)

Last week I had the pleasure of speaking at the 36th International Colloquium on Group Theoretical Methods in Physics (Group36) in Valladolid, presenting joint work with Arthemy Kiselev on const(p), the universal constant that appears when alternating compositions of weighted differential operators reduce to a Wronskian (arXiv:2605.11137, OEIS A392714 - all computed values always available at kianshah.in ). A huge thank you to the organizers for putting together such a stimulating week, and for making a place for early-career researchers among so many people whose work I've admired from afar. Looking forward to more insightful conversations at the GQT summer school and colloquium next month.
